info.name: UnifiedCare — Epic & Cerner EMR Integration (WSO2 Ballerina Healthcare)
info.description:
Demo flow for the UnifiedCare cross-EMR patient access API.

A regional care network runs its tertiary hospital on **Epic** and its community clinics on **Cerner (Oracle Health)**. The UnifiedCare API — built with WSO2's Ballerina healthcare connectors (`ballerinax/health.clients.fhir.epic`, `ballerinax/health.clients.fhir.cerner`) — exposes ONE API context over both EMRs: every patient operation fans out to Epic and Cerner in parallel and combines whatever each system returns. Authentication is **system-to-system (SMART Backend Services)**: private-key JWT for Epic, OAuth2 client credentials for Cerner. No user login, fully read-only.

Watch the service console while running requests — every EMR interaction is logged (request, HTTP status, latency, raw FHIR snippet, entry counts, cross-EMR link decisions) to show live connectivity.

Run top to bottom:
1. Unified lookup / search — one call, both EMRs, merged results.
2. Unified Patient-360 — aggregates clinical data where the id resolves, then demographically links and aggregates the same person's record in the other EMR.
3. Referral — pulls the packet from the source EMR and matches the patient in the target EMR.

Start the service first: `bal run` inside `unified_care_api/` (listens on port 9095).

variable.description: Camila Maria Lopez — Epic sandbox test patient (also has matching Cerner records)
Derrick Lin — Epic sandbox test patient
Nancy Smart — Cerner sandbox test patient (rich clinical record)
Joe Smart — Cerner sandbox test patient

item.name: 1. Unified patient access (one context, both EMRs)
Lookup by Epic id — found in epic only

request.description: One call fans the id out to BOTH EMRs in parallel. Epic resolves Camila Lopez (private-key JWT auth); Cerner reports a miss in `warnings`. `foundIn` tells you where the patient lives. Watch the console: both EMR round-trips are logged with status, latency and a raw FHIR snippet.

item.name: Lookup by Cerner id — found in cerner only

request.description: Same endpoint with a Cerner id (client-credentials auth). The API is EMR-agnostic — callers never need to know which system holds the record.

item.name: Unified search — merged matches from both EMRs

request.description: Searches Epic and Cerner concurrently and merges the results: Camila Lopez comes back from Epic AND her registrations in Cerner — the same human in two EMRs, combined in one response (`sourceEmr` marks the origin, `foundIn` lists the systems that matched).

item.name: Patient-360 by Epic id — auto-links Cerner record

request.description: Resolves the id in both EMRs, aggregates the clinical summary where it lives (Epic), then demographically links the same person in Cerner (family name + birthDate) and aggregates there too — `summaries` holds one Patient-360 per EMR and `linkedVia` explains the join. Epic's clinical sections appear as warnings because the sandbox app only holds Patient scopes.

item.name: Patient-360 by Cerner id — rich clinical record

request.description: Cerner-held patient: conditions, medications, allergies, vitals (component blood-pressure panels flattened) and labs fetched in 5 parallel Ballerina workers, plus an Epic demographic-link attempt. Allow up to ~90s — the open Cerner sandbox is slow, and its Condition search intermittently 504s (surfaced in `warnings`).

item.name: Refer Epic patient to Cerner clinic — MATCH_FOUND

request.description: Hospital (Epic) refers Camila Lopez to a community clinic (Cerner). The API pulls her record from Epic, searches Cerner by family name + birth date and returns matchOutcome MATCH_FOUND with the candidate Cerner patient ids. Entirely read-only.

item.name: Refer Cerner patient to Epic hospital — NO_MATCH packet

request.description: Community clinic (Cerner) refers a patient to the hospital (Epic). The transition-of-care packet carries the full Cerner clinical summary; the Epic demographic match returns NO_MATCH — a new patient for the hospital to register. Allow up to ~60s.
At least one of family / given / birthdate is required.
Neither EMR resolves the id → 404 with per-EMR reasons logged on the console.
